findings.evidence: "**Promotion:** seamless, powerful, innovative, vibrant, nestled, stacked praise." Current models already treat these words as press-release clichés.
findings.fix: Shorten the word list to one example. Keep the expert part: blatant press-release tone is an older-model signal, and current output promotes through award and coverage lists.

findings.evidence: "Diagnose in priority order: evidence risks ... first, then inflation and promotion, then structure, then vocabulary and mechanics." The process skill has no inline worked example of this ordering.
findings.fix: Add one short before/after pair under Workflow. It should show a vague attribution cut back to its supported claim before any vocabulary is touched, so the agent sees the evidence-first ordering applied.

findings.evidence: The over-correction gotcha ("Replacing every dash with commas and periods produces the over-uniform short-sentence rhythm that is itself a current cue") exists only in references/pattern-catalog.md. That file is not loaded for narrow edits.
findings.fix: Add one line to the 'Not tells' paragraph: 'Never mechanically replace every em dash or flagged word; uniform 8-20-word sentences are themselves a current cue, so vary the fix or keep the original.'

findings.evidence: "Use when a draft sounds robotic or the user asks to humanize text or remove AI writing patterns." It has no trigger for requests that never mention AI (salesy, breathless, cliché-heavy copy) and few keywords.
findings.fix: Edit existing drafts to remove formulaic AI-like prose, promotional filler, vague attributions, inflated significance and repetitive sentence patterns while preserving facts, quotations, author voice and house style. Use when a draft sounds robotic, generic, salesy or breathless, or the user asks to humanize text, make it sound natural, or remove AI writing patterns, chatbot phrasing, clichés or em-dash overuse, even without the word 'AI'. Not for authorship detection, factual research, translation, spelling-only proofreading, or writing from scratch.

findings.evidence: "make this paragraph sound more natural and human". All 21 queries are terse one-liners with no file paths, personal context or typos. Neither evals.json nor the trigger queries covers the reference-loading path (chatbot correspondence, disclaimers) or protected code identifiers.
findings.fix: Rewrite about half the queries with realistic context, for example 'my manager says ~/drafts/launch_post.md reads like ChatGPT wrote it, can u fix it'. Add an evals.json case with a chatbot wrapper plus an inline API identifier, asserting that the wrapper is deleted and the identifier stays character-identical.

findings.evidence: "Check before returning: every factual claim in the revision appears in the source; ..." The check has no failure branch. Separately, "Only a dense cluster of cues counts" (line 30) gives no threshold. For a paragraph with only 'serves as' and 'pivotal', the decision whether to edit is left to guesswork.
findings.fix: Add: 'If any check fails, revert that sentence to the original or cut the unsupported part, then re-run the check.' Define a cluster, for example: three or more distinct cues from different diagnostic groups in one paragraph, or one evidence risk alone.
